The footpath is broken in parts, blocked in part, is above the road level in part and completely gone in parts. Almost no pedestrian uses the footpath because you have to keep climbing up and down. There are open manhole covers on the road which makes it extra difficult. The road is very broad and some of it can be taken to create a safe footpath on the entire stretch

The bus stop is near a flyover and the nearest place to cross is at  Somajiguda junction where there is a break. There is a zebra crossing right after a flyover comes down on one side, and there is a free left at the zebra crossing on the other side. The vehicles never stop and it is very difficult to cross.

The footpath from Somajiguda circle to Greenland’s bus stop is broken in parts, has open manhole covers, and disappears in parts. There are also vehicles parked on the footpath despite parking available inside

The footpath on either side of Chief Minister’s Camp Office is blocked by transformers and poles, forcing pedestrians to walk on the road with whizzing traffic. Since it is a broad road, a new footpath can be constructed. This is particularly important to enable people to come for the open house conducted by CM

There is a zebra crossing on the road to Ameerpet but the zebra crossing ends at a permanent barricade, so you cannot cross safely. There is a overbridge on SP Road but it ends at the median and you have to cross the other side yourself. This is a high density area which needs better services.
There is no footpath on the service road below Begumpet Railway Bridge. There is a footpath under the bridge/ flyover, but that’s broken in parts, has open manholes and is blocked by a construction.

The footpath on Begumpet flyover disappears when you reach the level ground, so you are forced to walk between concrete bollards and rushing traffic. Also, there is no zebra crossing which enables you to cross the service road. This is critical because the flyover has a lot of pedestrian traffic

The entire stretch is virtually un walkable. There are no footpaths in places, the footpaths are blocked by political posters, the stairs to the overbridge takes up the footpaths. Even the traffic cops advise you to walk on the road.

There is an overbridge that leads till the median, but you have to cross yourself after that. 
Also, the bus stops are behind a barricade so you have to wait on the road.
There are a number of jewellary and clothing stores that use the footpath for valet parking. This can get dangerous for pedestrians
